# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 89 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 89 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_089_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 6

**1** "And the mountains — what are the twelve mountains?" I asked. "They are twelve peoples who dwell in the whole world. To these the Son of God was proclaimed by the apostles." **2** "But why are they different from each other — some rough and rugged, others without plants, others with thorns and thistles, others a desert, others with the greenest grass, others hilly, others smooth, others white — why are they so diverse?" **3** "Listen," he said. "These twelve mountains are twelve peoples. **4** The first mountain, which was black — these are those who have apostatized and blasphemed the Lord, and who have betrayed the servants of God. There is no repentance for these; therefore they are black, for their kind is death. **5** The second mountain, which had no plants — these are the hypocrites who have believed and who have no fruit of truth. As this mountain has no plant and bears no fruit, so these people profess the faith but have no fruit of truth in them. They are still capable of repentance, and if they repent quickly the death that was threatening them shall not seize them. **6** The third mountain that had thorns and thistles — these are those who believed, but became very rich and mixed with Gentiles. Many thorns and thistles were choking the herbs of their faith, so that they no longer bear fruit. These can come to repentance if they return quickly; but if they are slow, they shall die with the godless." **7** "And the fourth mountain that had many herbs, the upper part green and the lower part withered — these are the double-minded; they neither live nor are dead. They are like the wavering in purpose; neither dead nor living."

---

*EMET: the twelve mountains = twelve peoples/nations. The mountain typology begins with the worst (black = apostasy) and moves toward the best (green = virtue). "Double-minded" (dipsuchos) reappears.*
